madretsch.title: Madretsch Mosque
madretsch.excerptHome: Construction and development of the Madretsch Mosque, the Foundation's first major project.
madretsch.excerpt: Wakef Foundation's first major project: construction and development of the Madretsch Mosque in Bienne. A 496 m² space serving the Muslim community of Madretsch.
madretsch.subtitle: Wakef Switzerland Foundation's first major project
madretsch.intro: The Madretsch Mosque, inaugurated in 2009 in Bienne, is Wakef Switzerland Foundation's first major project. With its 496 m², it welcomes the Muslim community of the Madretsch district and forms the foundation on which Wakef built its expertise in Islamic financing in Switzerland.
objectifs: Create a dignified place of worship for the Muslim community of Madretsch
Provide a learning framework for Arabic language and Islamic education
Foster integration and coexistence in the local Bienne community
madretsch.description: As Wakef Foundation's first major project, the Madretsch Mosque testifies to the Foundation's capacity to successfully implement Islamic infrastructure projects in Switzerland. This project laid the foundation for our operational model: transparent community funding, professional management and strong local anchoring.
madretsch.avancement: Project completed and fully operational since 2009. The mosque welcomes the Madretsch community daily and serves as a stable landmark for the entire region.
madretsch.vision: The Madretsch Mosque remains a reference model: a place of worship well integrated in its neighborhood, serving a diverse and united community, symbol of the sustainability that Wakef Foundation seeks to embody.

aliman.title: Al Iman Centre
aliman.excerptHome: Islamic centre open to all nationalities: philosophy of total openness in the heart of Fribourg.
aliman.excerpt: Islamic centre operated by the Albanian Cultural Association (CCA), philosophy of total openness, transcending nationalities to welcome the entire Fribourg Muslim community.
aliman.subtitle: Islamic centre open to all nationalities
aliman.intro: The Al Iman Centre in Fribourg, operated by the Albanian Cultural Association (CCA), embodies a philosophy of total openness: transcending nationalities to welcome the entire Fribourg Muslim community. Built in 1997, it covers 132 m² in the heart of the city.
objectifs: Renovate and modernize infrastructure to better welcome worshippers
Provide a place of worship transcending national and cultural boundaries
Strengthen the link between the Muslim community and Fribourg society
aliman.description: The Al Iman Centre stands out for its philosophy of total openness: its doors are open to all nationalities and cultures, beyond the origins of the managing association. It is a place of meeting, learning and prayer for the entire Fribourg Muslim community, reflecting the city's cosmopolitanism.
aliman.avancement: Renovation work partially completed. Wakef Foundation accompanies the CCA Association in completing interior improvements and optimizing spaces.
aliman.vision: Make the Al Iman Centre a model of integration and openness, where the diversity of Swiss Islam finds its most harmonious expression, a community centre in the full sense of the term.

albadr.title: Al Badr Centre
albadr.excerptHome: Only mosque on the Franco-Swiss border: renovation of a historic 1902 building.
albadr.excerpt: Only mosque on the Franco-Swiss border: renovation of a historic 1902 building and 1,400 m² extension for a large Islamic cultural centre.
albadr.subtitle: The only mosque on the Franco-Swiss border
albadr.intro: The Al Badr Centre in Le Locle is a unique large-scale project: with land of 2,029 m², 600 m² already built and 1,400 m² for expansion, it is the only mosque on the Franco-Swiss border. The existing building, built in 1902, is remarkable for its architectural interest.
objectifs: Complete renovation of the historic 1902 building
Modern construction of a 1,400 m² extension
Create the only Islamic cultural hub on the Franco-Swiss border
albadr.description: The Al Badr Centre is Wakef Foundation's most ambitious project. Located a few steps from the French border, it serves a unique cross-border community. The project integrates the preservation of a remarkable architectural heritage (1902 building) with a resolutely modern vision for its extension.
albadr.avancement: Phase 1 completed: prayer hall for men (70 m²) and women (60 m²) operational. Phase 2 ongoing: complete renovation of the historic building and construction of the 1,400 m² extension.
albadr.vision: Make the Al Badr Centre a reference Islamic cultural centre for the communities of Le Locle and French border regions, combining heritage and modernity, in a unique location in Switzerland.

delal-el-khayr.title: Shades of Charity - Le Locle
delal-el-khayr.excerptHome: Acquisition of an investment property to transform into a multifunctional Islamic Centre in Le Locle
delal-el-khayr.excerpt: We are raising funds to acquire and renovate an investment property in Le Locle, which will become a comprehensive Islamic centre offering: mosque, training halls, residential units, and commercial space.
delal-el-khayr.subtitle: Multifunctional Islamic Centre
delal-el-khayr.surfaceDetail: 5 storeys · 6 apartments · 1 commercial unit · 5 parking spaces · 2 buildable plots
delal-el-khayr.intro: Wakef Switzerland Foundation is working to acquire an investment property in Le Locle, transforming an existing building into a comprehensive Islamic Centre: mosque, teaching halls, residential spaces, commercial unit, and developable land.
objectifs: Building acquisition: CHF 1'250'000 (CHF 550'000 to raise)
Renovation and adaptation for multiple uses
Creation of a mosque and prayer space
Training and educational halls
Residential spaces for caretaker and volunteers
Commercial unit generating income: CHF 49'380 annual net revenue
Two buildable plots for future expansion
delal-el-khayr.description: Le Locle needs a fully functional Islamic centre. This acquisition offers a unique solution: an investment property that partially finances its own development through rental income.
delal-el-khayr.vision: A welcoming Islamic centre: mosque, education, residential units, commerce, generating stable revenue for the Foundation and serving the Le Locle community.

annour.title: An-Nour Mosque
annour.excerpt: First Arabic-speaking mosque in the Valais canton. Phase 1 (210 m²) completed; Phase 2 (210 m²) ongoing with promise of sale until end of 2026.
annour.subtitle: First Arabic-speaking mosque in Valais
annour.intro: The An-Nour Mosque in Sion is a historic project: the first Arabic-speaking mosque in the canton of Valais, it responds to the needs of a community that previously had no suitable place of worship. With a budget of CHF 900,000 and an area of 420 m², this project unfolds in two phases led by the An-Nour Association.
objectifs: Offer Valais its first dignified and suitable Arabic-speaking mosque
Complete the two construction phases (210 m² + 210 m²)
Sustainably anchor the Arabic-speaking community in the Sion region

fiche.label: Phase 2
fiche.value: 210 m² promise of sale until end of 2026

annour.description: Valais is home to a significant Arabic-speaking Muslim community, long deprived of a place of worship commensurate with its needs. The An-Nour Mosque, led by the An-Nour Association with support from Wakef Foundation, fills this historic gap. Phase 1 of 210 m² is already operational.
annour.avancement: Phase 1 (210 m²): completed and operational. Phase 2 (210 m²): signed promise of sale, valid until end of 2026. Ongoing fundraising to finalize acquisition and works.
annour.vision: Make the An-Nour Mosque the spiritual heart of the Valais Arabic-speaking community, a space for prayer, learning and community life for present and future generations.

bibliotheque.title: Mobile Library
bibliotheque.excerpt: "Bridges of Knowledge": multilingual itinerant library promoting intercultural dialogue. Slogan: "Let's get to know each other. Knowledge brings us together."
bibliotheque.subtitle: "Bridges of Knowledge": knowledge brings us together
bibliotheque.intro: The Mobile Library "Bridges of Knowledge" is a unique project in French-speaking Switzerland: a multilingual itinerant library dedicated to intercultural dialogue. It travels to cultural events, public spaces and community venues to meet communities where they are.
objectifs: Promote intercultural dialogue through knowledge sharing
Make multilingual resources accessible to all communities
Train ambassadors of intercultural dialogue in French-speaking Switzerland
bibliotheque.description: Under the slogan "Let's get to know each other. Knowledge brings us together.", the Mobile Library travels through French-speaking Switzerland to build bridges between communities. The team of ambassadors carries not just books, but stories, languages, and the momentum of authentic encounters between people of different cultures.
bibliotheque.avancement: Active program since 2023. Regular presence at cultural events and public spaces in French-speaking Switzerland. Network of ambassadors in continuous development.
bibliotheque.vision: Make the Mobile Library "Bridges of Knowledge" a national reference for intercultural dialogue through education, leveraging the universal power of knowledge to unite.

hero.label: Pillar of Islam
hero.title: Zakat Calculator
hero.sub: Calculate your annual Zakat obligation according to Sharia rules. Current Nisab: CHF/€ 4,600 (≈ 85g of gold).

zakat.toolBody: Enter the value of your assets in CHF or euros. Zakat is due if your net wealth exceeds the Nisab for one complete lunar year (Hawl).
zakat.belowNisab: ℹ️ Your net wealth is below the Nisab (CHF {{nisab}}). You are not obliged to pay Zakat al-Māl this year.
zakat.nisabInfo: ℹ️ The Nisab is set at the value of 85g of gold (~CHF 4,600). Zakat is due if your net wealth exceeds this threshold for one complete lunar year (Hawl).
zakat.estimateNote: This calculation is an indicative estimate.

explain.title: The Nisab النصاب
explain.desc: The Nisab is the minimum wealth threshold. It is set at the value of 85g of gold (or 595g of silver according to schools). In 2025, this amounts to approximately CHF 4,600. This amount is revaluated according to the gold price.

explain.title: The Hawl الحول
explain.desc: The Hawl is the duration condition: your wealth must exceed the Nisab for one complete lunar year (approximately 354 days) for Zakat to be mandatory.

explain.title: The 2.5% rate
explain.desc: The Zakat rate on monetary wealth (Zakat al-Māl) is 2.5% of taxable net wealth, the total of your assets minus your short-term debts.

explain.title: What is zakatable
explain.desc: Zakatable: physical gold and silver, cash, bank accounts, stocks (market value), savings and Halal investments. Not zakatable: primary residence, personal vehicle, personal goods.

faq.q: Can I pay my Zakat in installments?
faq.a: Yes, Zakat can be paid in installments throughout the lunar year, provided the total is paid by the anniversary date (Hawl). However, it is preferable to pay it all at once to avoid missing a deadline.

faq.q: Zakat on salaries, how to calculate it?
faq.a: For employees, Zakat is calculated on net savings accumulated over a year, not gross salary. Calculate your remaining savings (income minus necessary expenses) after one lunar year. If these savings exceed the Nisab, you owe 2.5% of it.

faq.q: My calculator shows "Below Nisab", am I exempt?
faq.a: If your net wealth is below the Nisab (~CHF 4,600), you are not obliged to pay Zakat al-Māl. You can still make a voluntary Sadaqah at any time.

faq.q: Complex situations: entrepreneur, real estate, crypto…
faq.a: For entrepreneurs, owners of commercial real estate, investors or complex wealth situations, we recommend consulting a qualified Islamic scholar or our Sharia Committee. Contact us at info@wakf.ch.

zakat.noteBody: Our calculator covers standard cases. For entrepreneurs, commercial property owners, investors or atypical wealth situations, our Sharia Committee can guide you.

hero.label: Wakef Switzerland Foundation
hero.title: Frequently Asked Questions
hero.sub: All the answers about the Foundation, donations, Zakat and our projects. No answer to your question? Write to us.

items.a: Wakef Switzerland Foundation is a Swiss private foundation (art. 80 CC), registered under CHE-114.901.246, founded in 2009. It finances Islamic infrastructure projects in Switzerland: mosques, Islamic centres, scholarships and Muslim burial plots in cemeteries.

The Foundation is supervised by the Federal foundation supervision authority. It has an independent audit body that annually verifies the accounts and a Sharia Committee that validates the Islamic compliance of each project.
The initial endowment capital is CHF 50,000, in accordance with the statutes registered in 2009. All funds collected are added to this capital and used exclusively for the Foundation's projects.
You can donate via our online form on the "Make a Donation" page, by bank transfer (coordinates available upon request at info@wakf.ch), or by mail to our contact office in Bienne.

items.q: Can I make a recurring donation (monthly)?
items.a: Yes. You can choose a monthly donation by specifying your wish in the form. Our team will contact you to set up the automatic transfer.

items.q: Is the Foundation transparent in its management?
items.a: Yes. Wakef Switzerland Foundation is subject to Swiss civil law (art. 80 CC) and supervised by the cantonal foundation supervision authority of the canton of Vaud. Accounts are audited annually by an independent audit body and financial reports are available upon request at info@wakf.ch.

items.q: Can I make a donation dedicated to a specific project?
items.a: Yes. When you donate, you can specify which project you wish to support among our five projects: Madretsch Mosque (Bienne), Al Iman Centre (Fribourg), Al Badr Centre (Le Locle), An-Nour Mosque (Sion) and Mobile Library "Bridges of Knowledge". If the project is fully funded, funds will be allocated to the priority project in progress.

items.q: How do I calculate my Zakat?
items.a: Use our Zakat calculator available on the /zakat page. Enter your assets (gold, silver, liquid funds, investments) and short-term debts. If your net wealth exceeds the Nisab (CHF/€ 4,600) for one lunar year, you owe 2.5% of that amount.
The Nisab is the minimum wealth threshold. It is set at the value of 85g of gold, approximately CHF 4,600 in 2025. If your net wealth is below this threshold, you are not obliged to pay Zakat al-Māl.
Yes. Zakat al-Fitr is a mandatory charity given at the end of Ramadan, regardless of your wealth. Its amount is set each year by Islamic scholars (usually between CHF 10 and 20 per person).

Wakef Foundation finances five projects: Madretsch Mosque in Bienne (completed, 496 m²), Al Iman Centre in Fribourg (ongoing, 132 m²), Al Badr Centre in Le Locle (ongoing, 2,029 m²), An-Nour Mosque in Sion (ongoing, 420 m²) and Mobile Library "Bridges of Knowledge" in French-speaking Switzerland. See the Projects page for full details.

Each donation is allocated to a general fund or a specific project according to your choice. The Foundation Council validates the allocation of funds, and an annual report details the use of every franc collected.

items.q: Can I dedicate my donation to a specific project?
items.a: Yes. When you donate, you can specify which project you wish to support (Madretsch Mosque, Al Iman Centre or Al Badr Centre). If the project is already funded, funds will be allocated to the most urgent project.

hero.label: Official documents
hero.title: Foundation Statutes
hero.sub: The official statutes of Wakef Switzerland Foundation, registered under CHE-114.901.246 pursuant to art. 80 CC. Adopted on June 5, 2009, amended on April 13, 2018.

statutes.cardLine3: Art. 80 et seq. Swiss Civil Code · Head office: Prilly (VD)

articles.contenu: There is hereby constituted under the name "WAKEF SWITZERLAND Foundation" (hereinafter "the Foundation") a private foundation within the meaning of articles 80 and following of the Swiss Civil Code. The duration of the Foundation is unlimited.
The head office of the Foundation is in Prilly, in the canton of Vaud (Switzerland).

The Foundation aims to support and finance projects of a religious, educational, social and humanitarian nature, in accordance with Islamic values and in compliance with Swiss law. The Foundation operates exclusively in Switzerland. It pursues in particular the following objectives: (1) Build, purchase and renovate Muslim places of worship; (2) Contribute to the training of imams and their integration into Swiss society; (3) Support schools of Arabic language and Muslim culture; (4) Provide scholarships to Muslim students; (5) Encourage charitable, educational, scientific and sociocultural activities; (6) Support the creation of Muslim burial plots in Swiss cemeteries.

The endowment capital is fixed at CHF 50,000 (fifty thousand Swiss francs) in cash. The Foundation manages this capital according to principles of liquidity, security, return and risk distribution. This capital is inalienable and dedicated exclusively to the Foundation's purposes.

The Foundation's resources come from the endowment capital and its returns, donations and bequests from individuals or legal entities, subsidies granted by public or private organizations, and any other income compatible with the Foundation's purpose.

Members of the Foundation's governing bodies are liable for damages they cause intentionally or negligently in the exercise of their duties, in accordance with the provisions of the Swiss Code of Obligations.
The Foundation's governing bodies are: the Foundation Council (FC), the Management Committee (MC), also called the Board, the Working Group (WG), and the audit body.

The Foundation Council is composed of 7 to 10 members, all of Muslim faith. At least three quarters of members must be domiciled in Switzerland. Members are coopted by a two-thirds majority of serving members. Members exercise their duties on a voluntary basis.

The Foundation Council is the Foundation's supreme body. It is empowered to: define the Foundation's strategic direction, authorize acts of signature on behalf of the Foundation, appoint and remove members of the Management Committee, approve the annual budget and accounts, enact internal regulations, and any other decision reserved to the FC by these statutes.

The Foundation Council meets at least once a year. The agenda is communicated to members at least 30 days before the meeting. A quorum is reached when a majority of members is present, including the President or Vice-President. Decisions are made by a simple majority of members present.
The Management Committee (Board) is composed of the President, Vice-President and Secretary. Management Committee members are elected by the Foundation Council for a term of five years, renewable.

The Management Committee executes Foundation Council decisions and represents the Foundation in dealings with third parties by joint signature. It prepares the annual budget and Foundation balance sheet, and manages current affairs.
The Management Committee meets at least four times a year to handle current affairs and monitor ongoing projects.
Any Foundation Council member may oppose a Management Committee decision within 30 days. Opposition has a suspensory effect and the contested decision is submitted to the Foundation Council.

The audit body is external and independent of the Foundation. It is appointed by the Foundation Council for a term of one year, renewable. It verifies the annual accounts and reports to the Foundation Council and the supervision authority.

The accounting year covers the period from January 1 to December 31. Annual financial statements are submitted for approval by the Foundation Council within six months following the close of the accounting year.
These statutes may be amended by Foundation Council decision made by a two-thirds majority of serving members. The Foundation's purpose is immutable and cannot be amended.
The dissolution of the Foundation is governed by articles 88 and 89 of the Swiss Civil Code. It is decided by the competent supervision authority.

Upon dissolution, the Foundation's assets are transferred to one or more Swiss public law institutions or recognized public-interest organizations, pursuing an analogous purpose and tax-exempt. This clause is immutable. The founders irrevocably renounce any rights over the Foundation's assets.

The Foundation is subject to supervision by the competent authority in accordance with articles 84 of the Swiss Civil Code and 96 of the Commercial Register Ordinance (CRO). The Foundation may request an exemption from supervision in accordance with article 87 CC.
The Foundation is registered in the commercial register of the canton of Vaud.

sections.title: 1. Data controller
sections.content: Wakef Switzerland Foundation (CHE-114.901.246), Avenue de la Confrérie 11, 1008 Prilly (VD), is responsible for processing your personal data within the meaning of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the Swiss Federal Data Protection Act (FADP).

sections.title: 2. Data collected
sections.content: We collect only necessary data: first and last name, email address, phone number (if provided), donation amount and type, and any information you provide via the contact form.

sections.title: 3. Processing purposes
sections.content: Your data is used to: process your donation and issue a tax receipt, respond to your contact requests, send our newsletter (with your consent), and fulfill our legal obligations (tax, accounting).

sections.title: 4. Legal bases
sections.content: Processing is based on: your consent (newsletter), contract execution (donations), our legal obligations (tax receipts, accounting), and our legitimate interest (security and service improvement).

sections.title: 5. Data retention
sections.content: Your donation data is retained for 10 years (Swiss legal requirement). Contact data is deleted upon request or after 3 years of inactivity. Newsletter data is deleted upon unsubscription.

sections.title: 6. Data sharing
sections.content: Your data is never sold. It may be shared with: Formspree (form processing), Mailchimp (newsletter), and Swiss tax authorities (tax receipts only).

sections.title: 7. Your rights
sections.content: In accordance with GDPR and FADP, you have the right to access, correction, deletion, portability and opposition. To exercise these rights, contact us at info@wakf.ch.

sections.title: 8. Cookies
sections.content: Our site uses only technical cookies necessary for operation (no advertising or third-party tracking cookies). You can disable cookies in your browser.

sections.title: 9. Contact and complaints
sections.content: For questions, contact: info@wakf.ch · +41 79 379 96 46. You may also file a complaint with the Federal Data Protection Commissioner (FDPC).
